label: copy phase (after the first output)
explanation: Broad copy-phase feature: fires on about 93% of copy-phase steps (t > L, recall_idx >= 1) and almost never during the original phase or at the <DEL> step (0.1% of mass outside the copy phase, mostly weak firing on the last one or two original tokens of long sequences). Token identity barely matters (in_tok/out_tok/first_tok rates are flat). Strongest activations in the top examples come early in the copy phase (recall_idx 1-2, i.e. right after <DEL>) in short sequences, especially when the copied input repeats an earlier token; the firing rate is highest at recall_idx 2 (0.97). The ~7% of copy steps where it is silent are scattered, with no clear pattern.

issues: The main claims hold. On the test split, 'phase == 2' scores precision 0.930, recall 0.996, F1 0.962 and mass recall 0.999, matching the reported numbers. Firing outside the copy phase is about 9.9k steps holding 0.1% of the mass, almost all at orig_idx 7-8 (rates 0.019 and 0.076), so 'weak firing on the last one or two original tokens of long sequences' is accurate.

The silent copy steps show no systematic class. Firing rate by L x recall_idx stays between 0.84 and 1.0 everywhere except L=3, recall_idx 1 (0.67), and L=3 is rare. Rates are also flat for digit inputs (0.922), letter inputs (0.93), in_count>=2 (0.918), prev_tok==in_tok (0.932), the last copy step (0.936) and n_digits>=3 (0.875).

The magnitude claim is mostly unsupported, though the explanation already flags it as unchecked. Early copy (recall_idx<=2) carries only about 1.05x its share of active steps in mass (0.385 vs 0.368). L<=4 carries about 1.17x. Copied inputs that repeat an earlier token carry about 0.97x (in_count>=2 & in_first==0 & recall_idx<=2: 0.059 vs 0.061), so 'often where the copied input repeats an earlier token' is not borne out. The top examples share a different pattern: the next token to be output is 'f' (e.g. j v f f <DEL>, peak at v). For copy steps where next_out=='f', the firing rate is 0.991 against the 0.93 average and mass is about 1.45x its share of active steps, so 'token identity barely matters' has a small exception in magnitude.
The label 'copy phase (after the first output)' matches the predicate and does not overclaim.
